sections.overview: The Beautiful Woodpecker is endemic to Colombia and is confined to the Magdalena River valley.
sections.identification: The male has a red crown extending to the nape; the female has a black forecrown and red hindcrown, a pattern distinguishing it from the related Golden-naped Woodpecker (*M. chrysauchen*).
sections.habitat: It uses forest, forest fragments and, occasionally, plantations in the Magdalena valley.
sections.diet: It takes insects, including termites and beetles, and supplements them with fruits and seeds.
sections.behavior: It often forages in the middle or upper tree canopy, alone or in pairs, and calls from high branches.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific nesting details were not established by the regional sources consulted.
sections.ecology: Its diet links tree-dwelling insects and fruits to the food web of Magdalena valley forests.
sections.conservation: A 2024 Colombian endemic-bird atlas lists it as Least Concern nationally while documenting a restricted distribution and remaining forest cover.
